claims.summary: For every d>=3 in characteristic not two, the generic length-N Hasse kernel of the normalized n=5 two-pair conic limit, N=16d-16, is isomorphic to quartics Q satisfying the two Robin conditions at z=plus/minus1, two coupled value/derivative conditions at z=plus/minus i, and q4+u^N q0=0 specified in the source. The map is Q -> (z-u)^N(z^2-1)Q/[z^(8d-6)(z^2+1)], with an explicit five-by-five matrix depending on d.
claims.assessment: Working proof by a rational parametrization, the full ambient divisor, the earlier seven character conditions, characteristic-safe local coordinate changes and two eliminated value constraints. Six exact comparisons with the original growing Hasse matrix agree. This decides generic normality by a fixed-size determinant but does not classify its zero set.
claims.rationale: Makes the degree dependence of the conic normality criterion explicit and supports a uniform obstruction calculation. The earlier seven-functional reduction is credited; no broader novelty is claimed.
claims.next_action: Classify the identically vanishing determinants and retain a less degenerate normality route on the proved exceptional family.

claims.summary: In characteristic three, for every r>=1 put P=3^(4r), d=(P+15)/16 and N=P-1. The n=5 two-pair conic limit has generic length-N Hasse jet corank exactly one. In the quartic criterion its kernel is generated by Q=(z-u)(u^P z^3+1); the corresponding section has exact order P=N+1 at the generic mark.
claims.assessment: Working proof by Frobenius and explicit elimination of the five quartic conditions. It explains and extends the recorded d=6,p=3 exception to an infinite family (next d=411). It is a failure of a sufficient conic limit only; original cube non-normality, completeness of the exception list, and the entire generic order sequence are not asserted.
claims.rationale: Shows that the conic endpoint has infinitely many structural failures and supplies their unique missing section, so an all-degree proof needs a less degenerate mechanism on this family. No original cube conjecture is refuted.
claims.next_action: Determine whether the one-merge elliptic limit preserves the missing jet uniformly for this characteristic-three family.
